hero.subtitle: Websites, frontend, backend and CRM. From first sketch to shipped system.

manifest.body: Most people can build a page that looks good. Fewer build something that still works when a thousand people use it at once, when the payment has to clear, when the email has to arrive. I build the whole chain — the interface, the database, the login, the billing and the deployment.

work.title: Things I've built
work.intro: From NFC-linked SaaS products to client sites that actually generate enquiries.
work.allIntro: Seven projects, from fast client sites to platforms with payment flows and native apps.

services.title: What you can commission
services.intro: Four ways to work with me. Not sure which one you need — get in touch and we'll work it out.

websites.title: Complete websites
websites.summary: From blank page to a live site with its own domain, forms and analytics.
websites.detail: I handle everything: structure, design, content setup, development, accessibility, SEO and deployment. If you want to edit the copy yourself, I set up a CMS.
websites.who: Businesses that need a site which brings in customers, not one that merely exists.

frontend.title: Frontend
frontend.summary: Interfaces that feel fast, accessible and considered in every detail.
frontend.detail: React and Next.js with TypeScript. Animation where it adds something, never for its own sake. Accessibility and Core Web Vitals are built-in requirements, not afterthoughts.
frontend.who: Teams with design or backend in place that need the interface built properly.

backend.title: Backend & API
backend.summary: Databases, authentication, payment flows and integrations that hold up.
backend.detail: PostgreSQL with Prisma or Drizzle, authentication with NextAuth, payments through Stripe, transactional email, scheduled jobs and webhooks. Built to still be debuggable in a year.
backend.who: Products that need more than a contact form behind them.

crm.title: CRM & integrations
crm.summary: Systems that get your tools talking to each other instead of creating double work.
crm.detail: Custom admin panels, customer databases, automated flows and connections to the services you already use. This is often where the biggest time saving hides.
crm.who: Teams spending hours a week moving data by hand.

stack.title: What I build with
stack.intro: Everything below sits in at least one project running in production.

discover.title: Discover
discover.body: We work out what you actually need, who will use it and what counts as success. You get a fixed scope and a price before anything gets built.

design.title: Design
design.body: Structure and interface take shape. You see real drafts early, not a finished site you wish you had changed from the start.

build.title: Build
build.body: Development in short cycles with continuous check-ins. You can follow the work on a staging link the whole way.

launch.title: Launch & maintain
launch.body: Deployment, domain, analytics and handover. Then I stay available for whatever comes up afterwards.

cta.title: Tell me what you want to build
cta.body: A short conversation is enough to tell whether we're a fit. You'll get a clear answer on scope and price either way.

footer.builtBy: Built from scratch by me — Next.js, React Three Fiber and GSAP.

about.title: I build things meant to last
about.intro: I'm Oskar Östlind and I build complete digital solutions — from the interface people click on to the database and payment flow behind it.
about.body1: I started with Python and small scripts. That grew into Flask applications with users and payments, and from there into Next.js, TypeScript and native iOS apps. That path still shows in how I work: I want to understand the whole system, not just my layer of it.
about.body2: Right now I mostly build on Next.js with TypeScript, PostgreSQL and Prisma, with Stripe for payments and Capacitor when something needs to become a real app. But the tool is rarely the point — the point is that what gets built can be trusted.
about.body3: I work freelance and prefer to work close to whoever is commissioning. Short distances, fast decisions and a staging link you can follow the whole way.
about.toolsIntro: Grouped by what they do. Everything here sits in at least one project that's live.
